 =================================================================1700 1451   37
  Warning                                                         1700 1451   38
 =================================================================1700 1451   39
  MF/MT combinations used to define photoionization subshell cross1700 1451   40
  sections (MF=23, MT=534-572) and coherent anomalous scattering  1700 1451   41
  factors (MF=27, MT=505 AND 506) are newly defined MF/MT numbers 1700 1451   42
  for ENDF/B-VI that did not exist in earlier versions of ENDF/B. 1700 1451   43
  If you are not prepared to use this data you need merely delete 1700 1451   44
  it and all of the remaining data will still be consistent and   1700 1451   45
  equivalent to the types of data in earlier versions of ENDF/B.  1700 1451   46
  However, this will limit the range of problems to which this    1700 1451   47
  data can be applied (see: ref. 1 for details).                  1700 1451   48
 =================================================================1700 1451   49
  Definition of new types of data                                 1700 1451   50
 =================================================================1700 1451   51
  1) The total photoionization cross section is equal to the sum  1700 1451   52
     of the photoionization subshell cross sections.              1700 1451   53
                                                                  1700 1451   54
     For each subshell on the second line of a section the C1 and 1700 1451   55
     C2 fields are defined as,                                    1700 1451   56
                                                                  1700 1451   57
     EPE = The photoionization edge energy (similar to Q-value)   1700 1451   58
     EFL = The fluorescence yield (eV/photoionization)            1700 1451   59
                                                                  1700 1451   60
  2) The angular distribution of coherently scattered photons is, 1700 1451   61
                                                                  1700 1451   62
     S(E,MU) = 3*T/8*(1 + MU**2)*((FF(M)+F1(E))**2+(F2(E))**2)    1700 1451   63
                                                                  1700 1451   64
     S(E,MU) = Angular distributions (barns per unit cosine)      1700 1451   65
     T       = The Thomson cross section                          1700 1451   66
     MU      = The cosine of the scattering angle                 1700 1451   67
     FF(M)   = The atomic form factor                             1700 1451   68
     M       = Momentum transfer = SIN(THETA/2)/LAMBDA/4*PI       1700 1451   69
     F1(E)   = The real anomalous scattering factor               1700 1451   70
     F2(E)   = The imaginary anomalous scattering factor          1700 1451   71
                                                                  1700 1451   72
     F1(E) and F2(E) are isotropic.                               1700 1451   73
                                                                  1700 1451   74
     When F1(E) = F2(E) = 0 this reduces to the result obtained   1700 1451   75
     using only form factors (the older ENDF/B convention).       1700 1451   76
 =================================================================1700 1451   77
 Differences between EPDL97 and the data base presented here      1700 1451   78
 =================================================================1700 1451   79
 1) Energy range - EPDL97 - 1 eV to 100 GeV                       1700 1451   80
                   Here   - 1 eV TO 100 GeV (previously 100 MeV)  1700 1451   81
 2) Type of Data - EPDL97 - Photon interaction including          1700 1451   82
                            photoexcitation                       1700 1451   83
                   Here   - Photon interaction  - ENDF/B-VI has   1700 1451   84
                            no provision for photoexcitation      1700 1451   85
 3) Secondary E  - EPDL97 - Average energy of each secondary      1700 1451   86
                            (photons, electrons, positrons)       1700 1451   87
                   HERE   - No secondary energy data              1700 1451   88
 4) Interpolation- EPDL97 - Cross sections are Log X vs. Log Y    1700 1451   89
                            interpolable - the total cross        1700 1451   90
                            section is not included               1700 1451   91
                          - Form factors and scattering functions 1700 1451   92
                            are Log X vs. Log y, except first     1700 1451   93
                            interval.                             1700 1451   94
                          - Anomalous scattering factors linearly 1700 1451   95
                            interpolable (they can be negative)   1700 1451   96
                   Here   - Up through ENDF/B-V photon interaction1700 1451   97
                            cross sections were Log X vs. Log Y.  1700 1451   98
                          - For the first two Mods. of ENDF/B-VI  1700 1451   99
                            in order to consistently define the   1700 1451  100
                            total cross sections at ALL energies  1700 1451  101
                            all cross sections were linearized.   1700 1451  102
                            This was NOT a good idea.             1700 1451  103
                          - Starting with Mod. 3, cross sections  1700 1451  104
                            are left in Log X vs. Log. Y form so  1700 1451  105
                            that they are IDENTICAL to what's in  1700 1451  106
                            EPDL97.                               1700 1451  107
                            The total is defined ONLY at the      1700 1451  108
                            energies tabulated in any other cross 1700 1451  109
                            section.                              1700 1451  110
                 WARNING  - As a result the total cross section   1700 1451  111
                            MUST NOT be interpolated to define the1700 1451  112
                            total between tabulated energies. The 1700 1451  113
                            ONLY consist way to define the total  1700 1451  114
                            between tabulated energies is to      1700 1451  115
                            interpolate all of the partials and   1700 1451  116
                            add them up.                          1700 1451  117
